title.narrative: Girls trained who demonstrate digital literacy

comment.narrative: Year 5 target substantially achieved A decrease in the percentage of girls demonstrating digital literacy can be attributed to two main factors: (a) Some states have begun implementing more rigorous assessments of digital skills, which may result in lower reported proficiency rates as measurement becomes more stringent, and all states will be encouraged to review and update their assessments. (b) There has been a significant (74%) increase in the number of girls participating in digital literacy training programs. As these programs scale up, a learning curve is expected—both for participants and implementers—which may temporarily affect overall proficiency rates as new cohorts adapt to the curriculum and delivery methods.

title.narrative: Girls completion rate in participating states

comment.narrative: Year 5 target surpassed/fully achieved The decline in the value of this indicator and its sub-indicators is likely attributable to several factors. First, previous data were based on the 2021/22 Annual School Census (ASC), but since then, some states have conducted new ASC data collections, resulting in updated figures that reflect changes over the intervening period. Second, the rapid increase in girls enrollment in Junior and Senior Secondary Schools (JSS and SSS) since the project began may have contributed to a lower completion rate. This is because higher enrollment can lead to more students registering but also dropping out, or because newly enrolled students may lack the necessary support or foundational knowledge to complete their studies. Moving forward, HOPE will support the ASC in participating states, so we anticipate more recent and accurate data being made available before Project closing.

title.narrative: Girls currently enrolled in JSS and SSS in participating states

comment.narrative: Progress is on track, and the Year 5 target is surpassed/fully achieved. During the June 2025 ISR, some states relied on outdated ASC reports. In addition, some states reported cumulative totals rather than current figures. The decline observed in the latest report was a result of realignment between their data sources and verifiable information. States without recent ASC relied on updated EMIS data and ensured they report current figures rather than cumulative totals, resulting in a more accurate reflection of the actual situation.
